title: LTS Channel Compatibility Map and Silent Upgrade Orchestrator
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design a cross-surface LTS channel compatibility map and implement a small prototype of a 'silent upgrade orchestrator' that enables staged, reversible upgrades across runtime, API, SDKs, and console with minimal customer disruption. This ticket captures the policy decisions, compatibility constraints, rollout gate definitions, and the short-term automation required for safe silent upgrades in Dedicated and Private deployments. The goal is to make upgrades predictable while providing teams with automated preflight checks and fast rollback hooks.
objective: Produce a supported-versions matrix that explicitly defines allowed version skew and behavioral contracts between runtime, API, SDKs, and console; deliver a prototype orchestrator that runs preflight validations, performs canary cohort promotions, and executes safe rollbacks based on SLO and functional checks.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility map document completed and reviewed by Runtime, API, SDK, and Console leads
Allowed version skew rules defined for each surface and encoded as machine-readable policies
Prototype silent-upgrade orchestrator can run a staged upgrade: canary (5%), ramp (25%), full rollout with automated rollback on defined failure signals
Preflight suite of compatibility tests (contract, end-to-end smoke, KV-cache replay) integrated into orchestrator and passing in CI for target minor-version pairs
Runbook and rollback playbook documented and linked from Console release page
Small-scale private deployment upgrade executed in staging with no customer-facing errors and post-upgrade metrics within SLOs
rollout_gates: Preflight: contract checks (OpenAPI/protobuf), semantic schema diffs, SDK surface diff reports
Performance smoke: 95th percentile token latency within 1.5x baseline for a representative workload
Behavioral smoke: 20 canonical prompt/eval set pass rate within 98% of baseline
Observability: tracing and token-level cost events are present and mapped to new runtime version
Canary cohort: 5% of traffic for 2 hours with anomaly detection (error rate, latency, quality metrics), manual approval if anomalies are ambiguous
Ramp gate: automatic step-up to 25% then 100% if no gate breaches; each step requires at least 30 minutes of stable telemetry
Rollback triggers: sustained error rate > 0.5% above baseline for 5 minutes OR quality regression > 2% on canonical evals OR severe latency spike beyond configured SLO breach
upgrade_tooling: orchestrator-cli prototype (go binary) that accepts 'plan -> apply -> promote -> rollback' commands
policy-store: YAML policies describing allowed surface skews, semantic break levels, and required gates
preflight-suite container with contract-checker, e2e-smoke harness, kv-replay test
canary-controller integrated with traffic-router to cohort by customer tags/region/plan
post-upgrade validator that runs targeted convergence checks (KV cache hit-rates, attention kernel fallbacks, token-cost deltas)
GitHub Actions job to run preflight against release branch and produce a 'compatibility report' artifact
Console integration: release page button 'Run LTS preflight' that triggers orchestrator via internal API
support_matrix_summary: Channels: LTS-Stability (3-year support), LTS-Maintenance (18-month security fixes), Fast (monthly feature), Experimental (no guarantees)
Runtime policy: maintain ABI within minor-version; major version required for ABI-breaking kernel or kv-cache format changes
API policy: backward-compatible additions allowed; removals require major or coordinated deprecation cycle with SDKs and Console
SDKs policy: allow +/-1 minor skew for runtime bindings; older SDKs will receive compatibility shims documented in release notes
Console policy: must be compatible with API minor versions within +2/-1; Console feature flags used to hide unsupported surfaces

Cross-surface rule: any change classified as 'behavioral' (changes to generation tokenization, defaults, or response schema) requires coordinated preflight across all surfaces and a documented rollout plan
compatibility_matrix_rows: Row: LTS-Stability | Support window: 36 months | Runtime: security+perf backports | API: guaranteed minor compatibility | SDKs: supported +/-1 minor | Console: supported with feature flags
Row: LTS-Maintenance | Support window: 18 months | Runtime: security backports only | API: compatibility patches only | SDKs: security patches available | Console: maintenance bug fixes
Row: Fast | Support window: rolling monthly | Runtime: new features allowed | API: new endpoints allowed, minor deprecations with 30d notice | SDKs: bump-to-latest recommended
Row: Experimental | Support window: ephemeral | Runtime/API/SDK: no stability guarantee | Console: hidden behind feature gate
matrix_policies_examples: Example: Runtime 1.20 (LTS-Stability) can serve API minor 1.20 and 1.21 requests but will reject API 1.22 if schema introduces removal of fields without deprecation
Example: SDK python v1.19 will be able to function with Runtime 1.20 via shim if only additive API changes occurred; breaking behavioral changes require SDK release or runtime feature-flag
Example: Console 2.5 can operate against API 2.4 and 2.5; Console 2.5 must enable 'legacy-templates' flag when interacting with API 2.4 to avoid UI regressions

2025-12-08: Prototype plan approved by Eng and Product; next step: implement preflight-suite and policy-store MVP
risks: Risk: Behavioral regressions are hard to detect with synthetic prompts — mitigated by adding customer-sourced canaries
Risk: Skewed SDK adoption (customers pin older SDKs) may block automatic upgrades — mitigated by explicit opt-out and staged invites to upgrade
Risk: Cross-surface coordination overhead — mitigate by provide 'one-click coordinated preflight' in Console and runbook templates
Risk: Orchestrator faults causing partial rollouts — mitigate with idempotent apply/rollback and strong telemetry safeguards
